title: Rudolf Flesch and the Birth of Readability Formulas
explainer: In the 1940s, Rudolf Flesch developed a mathematical formula - based on measures like average sentence length and syllables per word - to predict how difficult a piece of writing is for a reader, work that grew into the Flesch Reading Ease test and, later with J. Peter Kincaid, the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level test. These formulas gave the intuitive advice to 'write shorter sentences in plainer words' an empirical basis, and they are still built into word processors and technical-writing style checkers today. Flesch went on to advise U.S. agencies on plain-language writing, connecting this research directly to the plain-language principles this lesson teaches.
